#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a dated tarball and copies it to the
# backup destination.
#
# The destination is environment-specific and must be supplied by whoever
# runs/schedules this job. It is read from the BACKUP_DEST environment
# variable (preferred) or from a "backup-dest.conf" file next to this script
# containing a single line with the destination.
#
# Supported destination forms:
#   /local/or/mounted/path        -> copied with cp
#   user@host:/remote/path        -> copied with scp
#   rsync://... or host::module   -> copied with rsync
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
CONF_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/backup-dest.conf"

DEST="${BACKUP_DEST:-}"
if [ -z "$DEST" ] && [ -f "$CONF_FILE" ]; then
    DEST=$(sed -e 's/#.*//' -e '/^[[:space:]]*$/d' "$CONF_FILE" | head -n1)
fi

if [ -z "$DEST" ]; then
    echo "backup.sh: ERROR: no backup destination configured." >&2
    echo "  Set the BACKUP_DEST environment variable, or create" >&2
    echo "  '$CONF_FILE' containing the destination path." >&2
    exit 1
fi

STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/

case "$DEST" in
    *://*)
        # rsync URL form, e.g. rsync://host/module/path
        rsync -a "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"
        ;;
    *:*)
        # host::module or user@host:/path form
        case "$DEST" in
            *::*)
                rsync -a "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"
                ;;
            *)
                scp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"
                ;;
        esac
        ;;
    *)
        # Local path or mount point.
        mkdir -p "$DEST"
        cp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        ;;
esac

echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"
